finding.otx.malicious: AlienVault OTX: the domain appears in {pulses} threat list(s), several of which name malware or threat actors ({malware}).
finding.otx.suspicious: AlienVault OTX: the domain is cited in {pulses} threat list(s) with threat indicators ({tags}).
module.otx.checks: Queries AlienVault OTX (LevelBlue): threat lists ("pulses") citing the domain or IP, tags, malware families, whitelisted popular domains and passive DNS (with a key).
module.otx.fix:
Open your domain's page on otx.alienvault.com and read the threat lists ("pulses") that cite it: author, date, tags, malware families or named actor, role given to the domain (distribution, command and control, phishing).
Work out whether these lists concern you: a domain bought or expired then re-registered (lists older than your acquisition), an abandoned subdomain taken over by a third party, or a domain name contacted by malware without any compromise on your side. Compare the dates of the lists with your registration date for the domain.
If the indicators are recent, look for a compromise: unknown files, scripts, redirects or pages on the site, unknown administrator or FTP accounts, suspicious processes or scheduled tasks on the server. Remove them, restore a clean backup, update everything and change the passwords and keys.
Delete orphaned DNS records (CNAME to a terminated service, address of a former server) so that no third party can take over a subdomain, and revoke access to services you no longer use.
Cross-check with the other reputation sources in DomainRecon (VirusTotal, Google Safe Browsing, urlscan.io): a flag confirmed elsewhere points to a real compromise to handle first.
If a list is outdated or wrong, contact its author or OTX support with a justification (domain acquisition date, proof of cleanup, screenshots, logs).
Run the DomainRecon scan again. A mere citation without threat indicators (large well-known domain, whitelisted) is not counted: only malware, actors or threat tags matter.
module.otx.title: AlienVault OTX reputation
module.otx.why: OTX lists community-shared indicators of compromise: appearing there with associated malware flags a domain used in attacks, whereas a mere citation of a large site has no such value and is not counted.
